cues: A strong acid is fully ionised, so hydrogen ion equals concentration times basicity.
A weak acid gives the square root of K a C, which in logs is half of p K a minus log C. Bases work the same way through hydroxide, then p H is fourteen minus p O H.
text: Four formulas cover every case. A strong acid is fully ionised, so hydrogen ion equals concentration times basicity. A weak acid gives the square root of K a C, which in logs is half of p K a minus log C. Bases work the same way through hydroxide, then p H is fourteen minus p O H.
